identification.summary: Storm-0288 is Microsoft's designator for an actor that Microsoft's naming map associates with FIN8 [S8]. A 2024 Blackpoint Cyber incident write-up also describes FIN8 as known as Storm-0288 [S1]. MITRE describes FIN8 as a financially motivated group active since at least January 2016, targeting hospitality, retail and other sectors, which shifted in June 2021 from point-of-sale (POS) targeting to distributing ransomware variants [S2]. Symantec tracks the same group as Syssphinx [S3].
identification.firstObserved: MITRE: active since at least January 2016 [S2].
identification.notes: Microsoft status for Storm-0288 is 'group in development' in the naming map [S8]. Aliases stated in sources: FIN8 [S8], Syssphinx (Symantec) [S3], G0061 (MITRE) [S2]. Sophos tracked a Citrix NetScaler cluster as STAC4663 and described it as suspected to be linked to FIN8; this is a separate vendor cluster and its facts are not merged into FIN8 here [S5]. Symantec attributes the ransomware family it calls Noberus (BlackCat/ALPHV) to a different group (Coreid); FIN8 is described only as a deployer of it [S3].

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor is stated in the sources gathered; the actor is described as financially motivated [S2][S3].
attribution.confidence: Sophos-reported STAC4663 activity is described in coverage as suspected FIN8-linked (no confidence level confirmed) [S5]. Blackpoint attributed a 2024 intrusion to FIN8 / Storm-0288 [S1]. Microsoft's naming map lists the Storm-0288 to FIN8 correspondence [S8]. No government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: Vendor tooling and TTP overlap: BADHATCH and Sardonic lineage (Bitdefender 2021) [S4], Syssphinx ransomware-era reporting (Symantec 2023) [S3]. The Storm-0288 to FIN8 mapping itself comes from Microsoft's published map [S8]; Microsoft has not published a profile in the sources reviewed.

objectives: Financial gain: historically theft of payment-card data from POS systems [S2]; since 2021 deployment of ransomware, including BlackCat/ALPHV attempts reported by Symantec [S2][S3].

sectors: Other sectors including insurance, technology and chemicals (secondary coverage)
regions: United States (financial institution targeted in the Sardonic incident) [S4]
targeting.notes: Hospitality, retail and POS targeting per MITRE [S2]. A US financial institution was targeted in 2021 [S4]. Some outlets list insurance, retail, technology and chemical firms as broader targets; this was not verified against a primary report [S4]. Region data is thin.

capabilities.summary: BADHATCH reverse shell evolved into the Sardonic backdoor, which is extensible without redeploying components [S4]. Living-off-the-land use of PowerShell and WMI, with WMI event subscriptions for persistence and Plink for RDP tunneling [S4]. Ransomware deployment: Ragnar Locker (June 2021), White Rabbit (January 2022) and attempted BlackCat/ALPHV (December 2022) per Rewterz's summary of Symantec; Symantec reports a revamped Sardonic written in C rather than C++ [S3]. A 2024 Blackpoint incident used RDP from a compromised machine with a hijacked privileged support account, with possible AnyDesk and TightVNC use [S1]. Sophos-reported STAC4663 activity exploited Citrix NetScaler CVE-2023-3519 using PHP web shells, obfuscated PowerShell and BlueVPS staging [S5].

campaigns.name: Shift to ransomware
campaigns.summary: MITRE notes researchers detected FIN8 moving from POS targeting to distributing ransomware variants; Rewterz summarizing Symantec lists Ragnar Locker in June 2021.

campaigns.name: Sardonic backdoor in failed attack on US financial institution
campaigns.summary: Bitdefender disclosed Sardonic after investigating an attempted compromise of an unnamed US financial institution; lateral movement to domain controllers failed because malicious command lines were blocked.

campaigns.name: White Rabbit ransomware
campaigns.summary: Per Rewterz's summary of Symantec, FIN8 used White Rabbit ransomware in January 2022.

campaigns.name: Attempted BlackCat/ALPHV deployment with revamped Sardonic
campaigns.summary: Symantec observed Syssphinx attempting to deploy BlackCat in December 2022, using a Sardonic variant rewritten in C; reported July 2023.

campaigns.name: Citrix NetScaler CVE-2023-3519 exploitation (STAC4663)
campaigns.summary: Sophos reported STAC4663 exploitation of unpatched NetScaler systems was suspected to be linked to FIN8. Fox-IT separately reported opportunistic exploitation dropping web shells; that Fox-IT activity is not attributed to FIN8 in the sources.

campaigns.name: Blackpoint-observed FIN8 / Storm-0288 intrusion
campaigns.summary: Blackpoint's SOC detected RDP from a compromised machine using a hijacked privileged support account and stopped the intrusion; month of publication not confirmed.

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated group tracked as FIN8 (Mandiant/FireEye), Syssphinx (Symantec) and Storm-0288 (Microsoft naming map) [S1][S3][S8].
diamond.capability: BADHATCH, Sardonic, ransomware deployment, PowerShell/WMI living-off-the-land, RDP tunneling [S3][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Legitimate sslip.io service used in Sardonic-era activity [S4]; BlueVPS staging in STAC4663 activity (Sophos cluster) [S5]; Plink and RDP tunneling [S4]. Specific C2 infrastructure not captured.
diamond.victim: Retail, hospitality and entertainment POS environments [S2]; a US financial institution [S4]; organizations with unpatched Citrix NetScaler (STAC4663) [S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Criminal monetization rather than state espionage; no state sponsor identified in the sources [S2][S3].
diamond.technology: POS terminals, Windows enterprise networks (PowerShell, WMI, RDP), and internet-facing Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway appliances [S4][S5].

gaps: No Microsoft Threat Intelligence profile for Storm-0288 was found; the Storm-0288 to FIN8 mapping rests on Microsoft's naming map [S8] and a Blackpoint statement [S1]. Microsoft marks the group 'in development'.
The STAC4663 (Sophos) to FIN8 link is suspected-link only; Fox-IT's CVE-2023-3519 campaign is a separate observation and should not be treated as FIN8 [S5].

WebFetch could not reach any host in this session, so all reporting is taken from search-result summaries; the original FireEye/Mandiant 2016 report, Symantec, Bitdefender, Gigamon, Sophos and Blackpoint primary pages were not opened.
Blackpoint 2024 publication month and victim sector not confirmed; Sophos/Fox-IT article months only approximately dated.
Exact exploited vulnerabilities, ransom amounts, victim counts and recent (2025-2026) activity are not established.
ATK 113 alias and broader sector lists come from secondary aggregators and are unverified.

Removed unverified claims: 2016 PUNCHBUGGY/PUNCHTRACK campaign, 2019 BADHATCH observation and Dec 2020/Jan 2021 update dates, and ATK 113 alias, whose sources (ETDA, Bitdefender blog URLs) were not seen in search results; search results also placed Bitdefender's BADHATCH finding in March 2021.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain for this actor is POS and payment systems, Windows administrative paths (RDP, privileged support accounts, WMI) and internet-facing remote-access appliances such as Citrix NetScaler [S1][S4][S5]. STEP 2: The actor is financially motivated and evolved from card theft to ransomware, so it is relevant to DoD primarily through contractor, installation-services, lodging and retail/exchange payment environments rather than as a military-intelligence threat [S2][S3]. STEP 3: Observed pattern is phishing or exposed-service exploitation, then BADHATCH/Sardonic implant, living-off-the-land lateral movement and RDP tunneling, then ransomware [S3][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued opportunistic ransomware or card-theft intrusions against commercial hospitality, retail and finance entities [S2][S3]. MDCOA is ransomware against a DoD-supporting commercial service provider (billing, lodging, exchange or logistics) that disrupts mission support [S3]. Candidate indicators: WMI event subscriptions, Plink/RDP tunneling scripts, RDP sessions using privileged support accounts from unmonitored hosts, sslip.io lookups, and web shells on NetScaler appliances [S1][S4][S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track ransomware-linked reporting on FIN8/Syssphinx/Storm-0288 for commercial providers supporting installations; keep naming straight across Microsoft, Symantec, Sophos and Blackpoint clusters [S1][S3][S5]. (2) Authorities: response is largely on commercial or DIB networks, so coordination runs through DC3/DIB CS and law enforcement rather than direct military action. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize patching of internet-facing remote-access gateways, restrict RDP from unmanaged hosts and audit privileged support accounts [S1][S5]. (4) Coordination: share detection content for WMI persistence and RDP tunneling with sector partners and service providers [S4].
